title: Adaptive brand overlay & component-bleed controls for dense console panels
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Branded console variants currently apply brand anchor colors directly to surface tokens which causes visual "bleed" into small UI chrome (icon strokes, table gridlines, chart sparkline strokes) and produces contrast failures in dark/dense panel modes. Goal: introduce an adaptive brand overlay layer and per-component bleed controls so brand accents can be expressive at large scale (headers, banners) while preserving micro-component legibility and SLO-friendly rendering costs. Deliver a token mapping strategy, component override contract, and a small set of runtime flags for Private/Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a brand-overlay token layer that can be toggled on/off without rebuilding components
Default per-component bleed rules: none | subtle | full, respected by buttons, tables, chart strokes, avatars
Visual diff baseline coverage for top 20 screens in Console across light/dark/brand variants
No new WCAG AA contrast regressions for text/icons after applying overlay in dark mode
Docs and SDK flags for Private deployments documented in console-2026.03 release notes
comments: 2026-02-26 Lina Chen: Initial exploration looks promising. Prefer an overlay token that composes via CSS variable pipeline instead of duplicating surface tokens across themes. Raised concern about icon stroke recolor in deep-dark modes.

2026-03-02 Marco Ruiz: Prototyped overlay as an extra token layer (brand-overlay-color + opacity set). Implemented per-component 'bleed' prop for Button and TableRow. See PR #1245 for implementation details and screenshots.

2026-03-04 Jonas Meyer (Engineering): Reviewed trade-offs. Using CSS variables avoids style recalculation at runtime for hosted, but Private on-prem older browsers need a small polyfill — noted in ENG-5010. Also flagged performance regression on list heavy pages; added perf test.

2026-03-06 Accessibility review (Lina Chen): Ran contrast checks. Default 'subtle' bleed fails icon contrast at 10px in dark-high-density on brand purple. Proposed fallback token mapping: icon-on-brand => surface-ink with a min-contrast clamp.

2026-03-08 Product review (Asha Patel): Live demo with partner customer shows brand banners work and tables remain readable. Customer requested finer control for chart series colors — added to scope as sub_issue.

2026-03-10 Design review (Lina Chen): Approved visual direction pending small token rename (brand-overlay-alpha -> brand-overlay-opacity) to match existing token naming. Assigned follow-up to update documentation and changelog.

2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Merged initial implementation behind feature flag. Visual regression tests added to CI (Percy). Next steps: extend bleed rules to charts and add canary rollout in Dedicated clusters. See rollout plan in drive link.
